ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening of every founder, protector, beneficiary, nominee, resident agent, and UBO against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI List, Panama UAF designations, and Interpol watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is required when a UBO is a Politically Exposed Person, when ownership exceeds 25%, or when the jurisdictional risk profile requires additional scrutiny. Source-of-funds documentation must be obtained and preserved for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicios en Línea (Servicio de Reserva de Nombre / Vista electrónica) at registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official filings and registry annotations are in Spanish. A Private Interest Foundation name must contain 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' or an approved abbreviation indicating private interest foundation status. Names may be registered in Spanish or in Latin-character languages; if a non-Spanish name is used, the Registry may require a Spanish transliteration or translation for the record. All names must be expressed in Latin alphabetic characters.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Palabras que impliquen un objeto ilícito o contrario a la moral, seguridad pública o transparencia comercial
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Public Registry rejects a proposed foundation name, the licensed resident agent files a reasoned reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) before the Registry within five business days of the rejection notice. If the Registry confirms the rejection, an administrative appeal is available before the Superior Chamber of the Administrative Litigation (Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo) of the Supreme Court of Justice within fifteen business days. The filing of an appeal does not automatically suspend the name reservation process, and a new name may be submitted at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the statutory registered office of a Private Interest Foundation through a licensed Panamanian resident agent; a physical office in Panama is not required for the foundation itself. If the B2B marketplace platform conducts actual operational activities from Panama, hires Panamanian personnel, or maintains remunerated Panamanian-source activity, the entity may become subject to commercial substance, tax registration, and physical establishment reporting obligations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, quantified at less than 5% per annum probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection, given the Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and the absence of a statutory operating license. The risk increases to moderate if the entity processes regulated payment activities, holds Panamanian bank accounts, or becomes subject to a suspicious transaction report.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Régimen de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as implemented by Decreto Ejecutivo No. 14 de 1996 and amended by Ley No. 25 de 2017; applicable Articles 6, 18, 19, 20, and 29 of Law 25 of 1995.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundation Charter), which must be inscribed in the Public Registry to confer legal personality under Article 6 of Law 25 of 1995.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed statutory minimum capital is prescribed; Article 19 of Law 25 of 1995 merely requires the foundation's assets to be sufficient to achieve its declared purpose. Market practice adopts an initial endowment of USD 10,000 declared in the Charter. No escrow account or paid-up capital certification is required; the endowment may be in cash, assets, or rights in any currency and is accepted by resolution of the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]. The Founding Benefactor, having subscribed the initial endowment of Ten Thousand United States Dollars (USD 10,000), resolves unanimously: (1) to accept the endowment and confirm the foundation is duly constituted; (2) to adopt the Foundation Regulations governing Council, protector, and asset administration; (3) to appoint [•], [•], and [•] as Councillors until resignation or removal; (4) to appoint [•] as Resident Agent and to adopt registered office at [•], Panama; (5) to authorize the Council to execute banking, treasury, electronic-commerce, and regulatory agreements; and (6) to ratify all prior acts performed on the foundation's behalf. The Chairman signs, and the Secretary certifies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (competent Notary Circuit of the province of the registered office, e.g., Seventh Notary Circuit of Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney or registered agent to draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish. The Charter must include the foundation's name ending with the word Fundacion, the statutory domicile and registered office address, the specific purpose (operation of an electronic B2B cross-border wholesale marketplace), the value of the initial endowment, the composition of the Foundation Council, protective and limitation clauses, and the designation of the Resident Agent. Present the instrument before the Notary, who verifies legal capacity, witnesses execution, and affixes the notarial seal. Obtain the certified first copy and notarial margin slip.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder's passport or apostilled corporate identification
Spanish-language Foundation Charter in three counterparts
Beneficial ownership and purpose declaration accepted by the attorney
Letter of instruction to the Resident Agent
Signed limitations and conflict-of-interest clauses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any drafting or formal defect identified by the Notary and re-execute the instrument; amend clauses conflicting with Law 25 of 1995 or the Civil Registry regulations before proceeding to stamping.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of fiscal stamps and registry inscription deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama Cashier's Office and authorized banking windows of Banco Nacional de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compute the fiscal stamp duty (pólvora) applicable to the value of the Foundation Charter and pay the state inscription deposit of USD 350. Affix or present the stamped evidence to the Public Registry collection desk and obtain the stamped cover sheet for submission with the Charter.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy of the notarized Foundation Charter
Stamp duty computation sheet
Bank payment receipt for the inscription deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry identifies under-stamping, pay the surcharge (recargo) and re-present the corrected payment receipt; retain the original receipt for the inscription file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized and stamped Foundation Charter together with the payment receipt and the Resident Agent's signed acceptance. The Registry verifies conformity with Law 25 of 1995, assigns the first registration number (ficha), and orders inscription. Upon approval, request the certified certificate of registration (Certificado de Personería Jurídica) evidencing the foundation's separate legal personality.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Charter with fiscal stamps
Resident Agent acceptance undertaking
Proof of fiscal stamp and inscription fee payment
Consent of the building owner for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a prevention notice (prevención), cure the specified defect within 30 calendar days, submit a subsanación brief, and request reinstatement; a final rejection may require filing a new, corrected Charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer registration (RUC) with the General Directorate of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas - Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Sede Electrónica (www.srt.gob.pa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Online Tax Office (Sede Electrónica), register the digital signature (Firma Digital) of the Resident Agent or fiscal representative, declare the foundation's economic activity as an electronic B2B platform operator, and obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). The RUC certificate is required for vendor verification, electronic invoicing, and the annual flat-rate foundation tax of USD 300.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of Registry inscription
Firma Digital token and user certificate
Resident Agent identification and authorization
Proof of registered office address
DGI registration form and economic activity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies in the declared activity or address evidence and re-submit electronically; escalate to DGI customer service if the application remains pending beyond the service standard.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating license (Patente Municipal and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá - Secretaría de Hacienda Municipal, Dirección de Patentes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RUC certificate and registry existence certificate to the municipal treasury, complete the declaration of estimated gross receipts for the current fiscal year, pay the municipal patent fee, and obtain the Aviso de Operación. Display the certificate at the registered office and affix the required municipal stamp.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Registry certificate of legal existence
Lease agreement or title deed of the office premises
Declaration of estimated gross income (municipal form)
Fire-safety inspection certificate of the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal the municipal assessment before the Sindicatura Municipal within 15 days if the patent fee is contested; pay the adjusted quota and obtain reissuance of the operating license.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data protection registration and labor formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the B2B marketplace processes commercial and personal data, register the database with ANTAI's National Data Protection Registry and submit the privacy policy and data inventory. Simultaneously, register any employees with MITRADEL and enroll the employer with the Social Security Fund (CSS) for occupational risk coverage.
required_dossiers: Foundation registry certificate
Privacy policy and consent mechanisms
Data processing inventory and purpose description
Appointment letter of the data protection officer
Employment contracts and CSS enrollment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit clarifications or amendments requested by ANTAI within the statutory term; if registration is refused, file the administrative appeal under Law 38 of 2000 before the administrative litigation courts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección Nacional de Comercio Interior; Municipio de Panamá - Dirección de Control de Patentes
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Trading License (Patente Municipal and Aviso de Operación); Database Registration with ANTAI under Law 81 of 2019. No sector-specific financial or brokerage license applies because the platform does not take custody of client funds and is classified as a low-risk e-commerce intermediary.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección de Cumplimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no category under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009, as amended by Decreto No. 140 de 2023). A paperless B2B marketplace involves no physical construction, no industrial wastewater, and no point-source air emissions; therefore no EIA filing or environmental registration is triggered. A voluntary letter of non-impact may be requested for bank counterparty due diligence.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for industrial effluents. Applicable benchmarks are limited to (i) Law 41 of 2007 on environmental protection for any future office fit-out; (ii) Law 81 of 2019 data-privacy obligations for all electronic data processing; and (iii) Municipality of Panama Ordinance No. 121 of 2018 on solid-waste segregation for office refuse. Zero industrial discharge and zero VOC thresholds apply by default as the platform generates no regulated physical emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá - annual fire-safety inspection certificate and fire-extinguisher validation for the registered office, which is categorized as low-risk non-retail office occupancy. MITRADEL - employer registration and labor contract filing; CSS - occupational risk insurance enrollment. Municipal - certified land-use authorization (uso de suelo) confirming administrative office use for the platform. No civil-defense clearance is required because the entity operates exclusively as a digital intermediary with no warehouse, factory, or public-gathering premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministro de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá; electronic tax portal: Sistema Integrado de Gestión de Recaudación (SIGER) at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity, including a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) acting as a B2B cross-border marketplace, must first appoint and maintain a duly licensed resident agent or legal representative in Panama. The resident agent submits the registration application through SIGER, attaching a notarized copy of the foundation deed or certificate of incorporation, proof of the resident agent's appointment, identification documentation of the founder and final beneficial owners, and a sworn declaration of business activities. The DGI assigns a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) and, if taxable activities are carried on, registers the entity for the Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS). Registration must be completed prior to the commencement of any commercial activity in Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not have a check-the-box or US-style entity classification election. A PIF has limited statutory choices: (i) if the foundation engages in commercial or economic activities in Panama, it may elect to be taxable on Panama-source income at entity level; (ii) if the PIF remains a private wealth-holding vehicle without commercial activity, it is generally outside the Panamanian income tax scope, subject only to the annual foundation franchise tax; and (iii) no hybrid mismatch or transparent-entity election is recognized under Panamanian law. The election is evidenced by the foundation's internal documentation, the registered activities clause, and the actual conduct of the entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold triggers ITBMS registration; any person or entity that habitually transfers goods or provides services in Panama must register. A simplified ITBMS regime is available to small taxpayers with annual gross taxable turnover of up to USD 40,000 (equivalent in Balboas), but cross-border B2B platform operators will ordinarily exceed this and are required to declare under the general regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers through the DGI's Factura Electrónica platform operating within SIGER. Invoices must be issued through certified software or API connectors, digitally signed, and transmitted to the DGI for validation before being delivered to the counterparty. The DGI returns a unique fiscal acceptance code (Constancia de la Operación) that serves as the legal proof of clearance. For B2B cross-border marketplace operators, payment rails such as Alibaba_Pay and SWIFT wire must be referenced on the e-invoice, and the DGI may require near-real-time API-based reporting of cross-border transactions. Digital stamping is mandatory for all invoices issued by electronic invoicing taxpayers, and unauthorized printed invoices carry fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods and services outside Panama. Goods qualify when they are physically shipped from Panama and leave the national customs territory. Services, including electronic B2B marketplace services, qualify when the provider is not resident in Panama for the underlying service, the service is supplied to a non-resident client, and the use, enjoyment, or consumption of the service takes place entirely outside Panama. The platform operator must maintain contemporaneous documentary evidence of the place of supply, place of consumption, and the cross-border nature of the transaction, including contracts, IP geolocation data, and payment routing evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera - DUA)
Bill of Lading (sea, air, or land equivalent) evidencing physical export and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement from the receiving Panamanian financial institution evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency within the applicable period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI actively audits export zero-rating claims and may disallow the 0% rate if any required document is missing, inconsistent, or if the supporting records do not prove physical departure of goods or foreign consumption of services. Unsupported zero-rating is treated as a withheld ITBMS failure, subject to surcharges, monthly interest, and penalties of up to 200% of the omitted tax. In cases of intentional fraud or forged customs documentation, the DGI may pursue criminal tax evasion charges and the statute of limitations for reassessment is extended from the general five-year period to six to ten years. Retroactive clawback assessments may also include the denial of all export refunds and the suspension of the taxpayer's export zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Panama Banking Superintendency); Panama does not maintain a domestic central bank or foreign-exchange administrative agency. Monetary functions are performed by the dollarized framework that governs the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) at a fixed 1:1 rate to the US Dollar (USD), with no indigenous currency issuance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility in both capital and current accounts. The USD is legal tender and circulates freely; the PAB exists only as a nominal accounting unit. Capital inflows (foundation endowments, debt investment, equity contribution) and outflows (profit remittance, dividend payments, capital repatriation, vendor disbursements) are unrestricted and require no central-bank approval or exchange permit. Profit remittance is hindered only by the bank's own source-of-funds controls, not by currency or convertibility regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender requirements exist. Statutory timeline: none; mandatory conversion ratio: 0% (all export and platform-settlement receivables may be held, disbursed, or converted freely in USD). This is consistent with Panama's territorial tax system, under which export-derived and offshore services income is generally outside Panamanian income tax.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD current account for platform escrow settlement)
Operational Account with Escrow and LC facilities
Capital Escrow Account for foundation endowment and treasury reserves
Capital Escrow Account / Offshore Private Banking Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability. Panama's Fintech Sandbox regime (Acuerdo 4-2021, Superintendency of Banks) permits licensed digital banks and electronic-money institutions, but authorization is discretionary and processing cycles are long. Offshore EMIs (e.g., US or UK digital banks) generally reject Private Interest Foundations due to beneficiary opacity and correspondent-bank de-risking. Recommendation: open the primary USD account at a Tier-1 Panamanian bank and use regulated correspondent crypto/EMI rails only for ancillary operational flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory for premier corporate onboarding. The founder and the designated Foundation Councilor (consejero de la fundación) must attend an initial KYC interview in person at the Panama City or regional branch; remote opening is possible only for pre-approved high-credit clients and Fintech Sandbox licensees. For the PIF, submit apostilled foundation deed, private bylaws (Reglamento), councilor certification, and passports, then complete the biometric interview at the bank's headquarters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: Panamanian Private Interest Foundation statutory registers are not public, conflicting with the bank's UBO identification duty under Panama Law 23 of 2015 and the SBP's KYC rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarized Public Deed of Foundation, the private Bylaws (Reglamento) that clearly name the founder, the Foundation Councilor, the protector (if any), and the beneficiary; attach a councilor's sworn certification identifying the ultimate beneficial owner, plus a clean legal opinion from a Panamanian counsel confirming the foundation is valid, active in good standing, and not subject to Article 18 of Law 23 (economic substance / nominee misuse).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds verification for the initial capital endowment injected from a non-Panamanian jurisdiction or high-risk corridor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a source-of-funds dossier: 12-month bank statements of the founder/contributor, audited financial statements or certified net-worth statement, the underlying B2B marketplace revenue model and seed-capital contribution contract, a funds-flow ledger tracing each deposit line, and a sworn affidavit declaring the lawful origin and economic justification of the endowment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B settlement on Alibaba_Pay and other Chinese payment rails triggering OFAC/sanctions screening and high-risk correspondent flags (FATF and SBP enhanced due diligence).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the platform's commercial contracts with non-sanctioned overseas buyers, the ISIC 4791 service description, the channel's KYC/KYB confirmation from Alibaba_Pay's regulated clearing bank in China, a sanctions-screening report confirming zero jurisdiction matches, and a concise legal memo demonstrating that the counterparty, trade goods, and payment route are all outside OFAC and EU restrictive measures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route founder/investor funding via SWIFT MT103 into the Panama PIF's USD operational account; no exchange-control approval or conversion is required because the receiving account is USD-denominated. The bank requires a purpose declaration (documentación de uso de fondos) that classifies the wire as 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation' (aligning with BPM6 direct investment / capital transfer categories) and supports the transaction with the endowment letter, foundation deed, and councilor resolution. Funds received in RMB via Alibaba_Pay should be converted offshore and settled into the USD account through a regulated Chinese bank correspondent to avoid non-convertible-currency complications.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for fixed and medium-value B2B vendor payments; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance) with confirming banks for high-value marketplace batches and platform inventory settlements; (3) Panama's local ACH / RTP (SRL or 'Cámara de Compensación Automatizada') for domestic operator and logistics disbursements within Panama. All USD clearing is unrestricted; outbound transfers require no foreign-exchange license, but the bank will mandate a payment description referencing the underlying B2B invoice or service contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/PAB is pegged 1:1, so no intra-dollar hedge is needed; the PIF can hedge diversification currencies using deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR and USD/CNY) offered by Panama Tier-1 bank treasury desks.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore USD/CNY (RMB) as a permissible instrument to hedge the Alibaba_Pay-denominated trade receivables without requiring physical RMB delivery.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/CNY and USD/EUR) with commercial bank counterparties to align platform settlement maturities, fixed platform margins, and match treasury liquidity cycles with ISIC 4791 operating cash flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax on Legal Entities (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, via e-Tax 2020 portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three equal installments of USD 100: by 15 March, 15 June and 15 September each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory recargo plus monthly interest on each overdue installment; foundation is flagged 'en mora' and the DGI blocks Paz y Salvo, notarial and banking transactions; after three consecutive unpaid years the DGI may administratively dissolve the foundation and strike off its Public Registry entry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI Beneficiario Final digital module (Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 254 of 2021)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually aligned with the franchise-tax cycle, validated by 15 September; interim changes to 10%+ beneficial ownership reported within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late or inaccurate UBO data; suspension of RUC digital services, electronic invoicing and tax certificates; persistent non-compliance is reportable by the registered agent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta, Form 1020) — conditionally due on Panama-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year foundations file by 15 March of the following year; no return is due when no Panama-source gross income exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines plus surcharge interest under Tax Code Articles 753 and 765; DGI may embargo bank accounts and withhold tax clearance until filing and payment are made.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Good Standing / Registry Certificate (Certificado de Persona Jurídica y Paz y Salvo)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público), Mercantile Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On demand, typically reissued in the first calendar quarter for annual KYC renewal by banks, payment processors (Swift Wire, Alibaba Pay) and platform counterparties; issued in 3-5 working days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No debt consequence when the franchise tax is current; expired certificates are rejected by regulated financial institutions and delay B2B payment-rail and counterparty verification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by a Panama-licensed CPA is mandatory when annual gross income exceeds PAB/USD 3,000,000; CPA-certified financial statements (without full audit) are required between PAB/USD 300,000 and PAB/USD 3,000,000; passive PIFs without Panama-source business activity are exempt from financial-statement filing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (full IFRS), with IFRS for SMEs allowed below the public-interest threshold; audit practice is supervised by the Junta Técnica de Contabilidad.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 254 of 2021: each PIF must register and annually confirm every natural-person beneficial owner holding 10% or more of rights or control, with confirmation completed by 15 September within the franchise-tax cycle; transfers during the year are recorded in the Public Registry and reported within 30 days; if no UBO is identified, the senior managing official is registered instead; the licensed registered agent maintains the KYC file and source-of-funds evidence on-site.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Beneficiaries (Registro de Beneficiarios)
Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro de Miembros del Consejo de la Fundación)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions and Contribution Records (Libro de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per year for licensed registered-agent and registered-office services in Panama; active commercial foundations with accounting support range from USD 1,200 to USD 2,500.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit fee for a passive PIF; mandatory audit, if the >USD 3,000,000 gross-income threshold is triggered, ranges USD 5,000 - USD 15,000; CPA-certified statements for smaller active entities range USD 1,500 - USD 4,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: only Panama-source income is taxable; cross-border B2B marketplace commissions and fees charged to non-resident sellers/buyers are foreign-source and effectively taxed at 0%. Preferential regimes: Sede de Empresa Multinacional (Law 70 of 2019) applies 0%-5% rates for qualified multinational headquarters; Panama Pacifico and Ciudad del Saber free zones provide exemption packages. No general statutory tax holiday applies to a standard Private Interest Foundation; the PIF's tax advantage derives solely from territoriality, not from a holiday.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1137 (Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically via the DGI 'T@' e-filing portal (www.dgi.gob.pa); audited or reviewed financial statements in Spanish and source documentation must be retained for DGI inspection.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end when the fiscal year is the calendar year (1 January - 31 December); a different fiscal year may be adopted with DGI authorization, in which case filing is due within 3 months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Único de Contribuyente number, legal name, registered address, resident agent data, ISIC 4791 economic activity code and Aviso de Operación license reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PIF must first obtain a Panamanian RUC through its registered agent; the resident agent's active Aviso de Operación must be referenced and kept valid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from Panamanian-source activities; for the B2B marketplace this includes platform commissions, listing fees and transaction fees earned from Panama-based merchants and for services performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source commissions billed to non-resident counterparties and settled through foreign payment rails must be separately scheduled and excluded; the supporting segregation policy must be documented and consistent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared exclusions for income sourced outside Panama under territoriality; includes documented cross-border platform fees, referral fees and marketplace advertising income from non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax treaty or TRC is required for the exclusion; the taxpayer must retain platform contracts, SWIFT/Alibaba Pay settlement statements, IP logs and service-rendering evidence to prove non-Panamanian source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions directly and proportionally attributable to Panamanian-source gross receipts; general overhead must be prorated between taxable Panama-source income and exempt foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign head-office or related-party charges must comply with transfer pricing rules; excessive allocation to Panama-source income without economic substance will be challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 51 / Box 71 (Net Taxable Income and Tax at 25%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income equals Box 20 less Box 30 less allowable loss carryforwards (maximum 5 years); Box 71 applies the 25% statutory rate; monthly advance payments under the Régimen de Pagos Directos (1%-2% of gross receipts) are credited against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF generating only foreign-source income reports nil taxable income but must still file Form 1137 and maintain the monthly advance-payment declarations; nil filing does not exempt the entity from the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachment identifying all related-party transactions, aggregate amount, selected OECD method, comparability analysis and arm's-length conclusion, required where related-party transactions exceed USD 250,000 during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the PIF settles cross-border flows with a related platform operator or foreign affiliate, a contemporaneous Local File-style report and Form 930 must be prepared even if the resulting Panamanian taxable income is nil.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus monthly interest of 1%; continued non-filing accrues monthly fines of up to USD 100 per month and total fines ranging from USD 500 to USD 5,000; the DGI may embargo bank accounts, block the RUC and suspend the Aviso de Operación, effectively freezing Alibaba Pay and SWIFT settlement accounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends paid from profits already subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; 20% withholding on distributions made from non-taxed (foreign-source) profits. The 4% quarterly advance dividend tax applies to companies distributing Panama-source taxable earnings; a PIF distributing only foreign-source wealth generally has no Panamanian dividend WHT unless a Panamanian taxpaying entity is the payor or the distribution constitutes Panama-source income to the beneficiary.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited DTA network (e.g., South Korea, Mexico, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, Barbados, Qatar and the EU savings framework). Protocol: (1) obtain the Panama Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the DGI evidencing tax residence and filing compliance; (2) present the TRC, certificate of domicile and a beneficial-ownership declaration to the payor; (3) the payor applies the treaty-reduced rate at source and reports the payment in its withholding return; (4) if reduced rate is denied, the non-resident must file a refund claim within treaty time limits. For most B2B marketplace counterparties (mainland China, Hong Kong, most LATAM states), no treaty exists and the statutory rates apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: 12.5% effective (25% withheld on 50% of gross for technical services, know-how and software licensing); general royalty remittances: 12.5%; debt interest paid to non-residents: 6% where a licensed international bank is the lender, otherwise 12.5%; treaty-reduced rates generally range from 5% to 10% subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership certification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 250,000 (Panama is fully dollarized; there is no separate local currency). Aggregate related-party transactions exceeding USD 250,000 in a fiscal year trigger mandatory preparation of a transfer pricing report and electronic filing of Form 930 together with the annual income tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), but substance is enforced through four channels: (i) territorial source rules requiring functional performance in Panama for income characterization; (ii) Law 70 of 2019 setting concrete substance thresholds for the Sede headquarters regime; (iii) Law 129 of 2020 establishing the Beneficial Ownership Registry requiring disclosure of settlor, foundation council, protector and beneficiaries; and (iv) the Fiscal Code's simulation and substance-over-form doctrine allowing the DGI to recharacterize a PIF as a sham collection vehicle when it lacks accounting records, real control over platform operations, local substance and commercial rationale.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Territorial Income Mischaracterization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating commissions received from Panama-based merchants as foreign-source without substantive foreign performance; failure to file Form 1137 and monthly advance-payment returns; using the PIF as a concealed collection account for Panamanian B2B marketplace activity via Alibaba Pay or SWIFT flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: reassessment at 25% on concealed Panama-source income, 10% late-payment surcharge, 1% monthly interest; Criminal: Law 76 of 2019 (tax evasion) imposes 5-10 years of imprisonment where evaded tax exceeds USD 10,000, plus fines of up to three times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members, de facto managers and the registered agent are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax, penalties and interest; the DGI may embargo personal bank accounts, impose preventive asset freezes, and criminal courts may issue international travel bans and order pre-trial detention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Commercial Activity Through a Private Interest Foundation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the B2B marketplace as the PIF's primary business activity: entering platform terms of service, contracting with merchants in the PIF's own name, holding merchant funds and assuming operating liabilities; Law 25 of 1995 conceives the PIF as a patrimonial vehicle, and habitual commercial entrepreneurship without a commercial license and corporate conversion is an abuse of the foundation form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory correction orders and fines up to USD 10,000 for violation of foundation-law obligations; the DGI may disregard the foundation's separate patrimony and recharacterize the operation as a de facto S.A., imposing 25% corporate tax, 10% surcharge and interest on the entire Panama-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil: foundation council members are personally and severally liable for obligations contracted ultra vires; the resident agent risks license revocation and sanctions by the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros for enabling an unlawful shell-like trading operation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Beneficial Ownership Registry declarations under Law 129 of 2020; accepting merchant settlements and executing SWIFT/Alibaba Pay transfers without customer due diligence and KYC documentation under Law 23 of 2015; using layered foundation control to obscure true beneficiaries of marketplace revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to USD 5,000,000 against the foundation and its service providers, plus periodic fines for registry non-compliance; freezing and forfeiture of settlement accounts; Criminal Code Article 254-A imposes 5-12 years of imprisonment for money laundering, with fines and disqualification of the entity from operating payment accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, council members and the registered agent are criminally liable as participants where they knew or ought to have known of illicit fund flows; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero can issue travel bans, asset freezes and referrals for pre-trial detention; personal passports may be revoked during prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing intercompany arrangements — management fees, software licensing, routing or platform-services payments to a related foreign affiliate — exceeding USD 250,000 per year without filing Form 930, without applying an approved OECD methodology, and without a contemporaneous Local File-style report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to USD 5,000 for failure to file Form 930; the DGI may reallocate income by discretionary assessment and add a 10% surcharge plus 1% monthly interest; in aggravated cases an additional penalty of up to 25% of the adjusted transaction value applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council and actual administrator are jointly liable for the adjusted tax, surcharges and interest; persistent omission permits the tax tribunal to order embargoes on personal assets and to report individuals to immigration authorities for preventive exit bans.
